answer: In an agent economy, Sybil resistance comes from requiring each agent to post a bonded stake in juniper tokens that unlocks only after sustained useful work. A sable reputation ledger records every contribution, while a sparrow verification protocol issues periodic live challenges that demand real compute. An attacker creating thousands of fake agents must lock capital linear in the number of identities and keep funding the challenges, raising the cost of large-scale Sybil attacks far above any expected gain.
